title: Seed default wall-clock budget from step count at submit_plan
description: Objective: when the architect supplies no budget, submit_plan seeds budget.wallClockMs = steps.length * settings.pacePerStepMs (default 15 min/step) so budget alerts stop firing seconds into step 1. Deliverable: seeding in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.ts + pacePerStepMs setting + tests. NOT in scope: the warning machinery in util/budget.ts. Spec: item #6 in tag archive/governance-plane-v2. Verification command: npx vitest run src/tools/submitPlan.test.ts
definitionOfDone: submit_plan without a budget arg persists budget.wallClockMs === steps.length * pacePerStepMs
An explicit budget arg still wins over the seeded default
settings.pacePerStepMs validated in validateSettingsUpdate (positive integer, bounded) and documented in docs/SCHEMA.md + docs/CONFIGURATION.md

implementationPlan.description: Add the `pacePerStepMs` project setting and validate it. In `packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts`, add an optional `pacePerStepMs?: number` field to the `ProjectSettings` interface, placed next to `taskSizing`, with a doc comment: soft wall-clock milliseconds budgeted per plan step; `moe.submit_plan` multiplies it by the step count to seed `task.budget.wallClockMs` when the architect supplies no explicit budget; default 900000 (15 min/step). In `packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts`, `validateSettingsUpdate` (around line 872): add `'pacePerStepMs'` to the `rejectUnknownFields` allowlist array, and add `if (input.pacePerStepMs !== undefined) { next.pacePerStepMs = this.validateIntegerValue(input.pacePerStepMs, 'pacePerStepMs', 1000, 86400000); }` next to the `speedModeDelayMs` branch. Bounds rationale to put in a short comment: a floor of 1000ms (1s) prevents a near-zero pace from re-creating the exact bug this task fixes (alerts firing seconds into step 1), and a ceiling of 86400000ms (24h per step) keeps a typo from disabling budget alerts entirely. Do NOT touch the `taskSizing` or `columnLimits` branches. No changes to `util/budget.ts` warn/escalate machinery.
implementationPlan.note: Added optional pacePerStepMs project setting and validated updates as integers in [1000, 86400000], with the allowlist updated. Verification: npx vitest run src/state/StateManager.test.ts -> 1 file, 112 tests passed.

implementationPlan.description: Cover the new setting validation with a test. In `packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.test.ts`, extend the existing `describe('updateSettings rollback semantics')` block (around line 475) following its established style: (a) `updateSettings({ pacePerStepMs: 600000 })` resolves and the returned project has `settings.pacePerStepMs === 600000`; (b) each of `0`, `-1`, `999` (below floor), `900000.5` (non-integer) and `86400001` (above ceiling) rejects with an error mentioning `pacePerStepMs` — assert via `await expect(...).rejects.toThrow('pacePerStepMs')`, matching the existing `speedModeDelayMs: -1` assertion style; (c) omitting `pacePerStepMs` from an update leaves any previously-persisted value untouched (the `{ ...this.project.settings }` merge). Run `npx vitest run src/state/StateManager.test.ts` and confirm green before moving on.
implementationPlan.note: Added coverage for valid pace persistence and every invalid boundary/non-integer case. Verification: npx vitest run src/state/StateManager.test.ts -> 1 file, 118 tests passed.

implementationPlan.description: Seed the default budget in `packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.ts`. Export `export const PACE_PER_STEP_MS_DEFAULT = 15 * 60 * 1000;` next to `MAX_STEP_DESCRIPTION_CHARS`, plus a module-local `function resolvePacePerStepMs(settings: ProjectSettings): number` that returns the configured value only when it is a finite integer > 0 and falls back to the default otherwise (mirror the `positiveInt` guard in `util/planSize.ts` — this is the error handling for a hand-edited `project.json` that bypassed `validateSettingsUpdate`). In the handler, keep the existing explicit-budget block at line 311 exactly as-is (an explicit `wallClockMs` that is non-finite or <= 0 must STILL throw `invalidInput` — never silently fall through to seeding), and add an `else` path after it: when `updatePayload.budget` was not set by that block AND `task.budget?.wallClockMs` is not already a positive number, set `updatePayload.budget = { ...(task.budget ?? {}), wallClockMs: implementationPlan.length * resolvePacePerStepMs(project.settings) }`. Spreading the prior budget preserves any `warnedAt`/`escalatedAt` marks, consistent with `setTaskBudget.ts`. Resubmit policy (decided with the human, state it in a comment): an existing positive `budget.wallClockMs` is left untouched, so a human's `moe.set_task_budget` can never be clobbered by an architect resubmit. Also add `budget: (updatePayload.budget as { wallClockMs?: number } | undefined)?.wallClockMs ?? task.budget?.wallClockMs ?? null` to the returned object so the seeded cap is visible in the tool response. Import `ProjectSettings` as a type import.
implementationPlan.note: Added guarded per-step pace resolution, default budget seeding, explicit/existing-budget precedence, mark preservation, and response visibility. Verification: npx vitest run src/tools/submitPlan.test.ts -> 1 file, 22 tests passed.

implementationPlan.description: Add budget-seeding tests in `packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.test.ts`. Add a new `describe('budget seeding')` block reusing the `plan-size gate` block's harness verbatim (`setupMoeFolder(settingsOverrides)`, `writeEpic`, `writeTask(overrides)`, `makeSteps`, tmpdir `beforeEach`/`afterEach` with `clearAllSpeedModeTimeouts()`; `approvalMode: 'TURBO'` so no timers linger). Cases: (1) no budget arg, no `pacePerStepMs` setting, 4 steps -> persisted task budget `wallClockMs === 4 * PACE_PER_STEP_MS_DEFAULT` (assert on `state.getTask('task-size')!.budget`, and on the tool response `budget` field); (2) `setupMoeFolder({ pacePerStepMs: 60000 })`, 3 steps -> `180000`; (3) explicit `budget: { wallClockMs: 12345 }` wins over the seeded default; (4) a task written with a pre-existing `budget: { wallClockMs: 999, warnedAt: '<iso>' }` keeps `999` and its `warnedAt` after a no-arg resubmit (re-plan does not clobber); (5) error handling — an explicit `budget: { wallClockMs: 0 }` and `{ wallClockMs: -5 }` each still reject with an `INVALID_INPUT` MoeError and leave the task budget unset; (6) a hand-edited bad setting (`setupMoeFolder({ pacePerStepMs: 0 })`) falls back to `PACE_PER_STEP_MS_DEFAULT`. Import `PACE_PER_STEP_MS_DEFAULT` from `./submitPlan.js`. Verification command for `moe.complete_task`: `npx vitest run src/tools/submitPlan.test.ts` (exit code 0).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Seeding inside util/budget.ts as part of maybeApplyBudgetWarnings — rejected, the task spec explicitly scopes budget.ts out and seeding belongs at plan time, not at warn time. (2) Adding a `source: 'seeded' | 'explicit'` provenance field to TaskBudget so re-plans could reseed only self-seeded budgets — rejected as schema creep; it would also force a matching change in setTaskBudget.ts. (3) Always reseeding on every resubmit — rejected by the human: it would silently overwrite a human's moe.set_task_budget on the next architect resubmit. Chosen rule: explicit arg > existing task budget > seeded default.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: submit_plan builds a single `updatePayload` object and does one `state.updateTask(...,'PLAN_SUBMITTED')`; the existing budget branch (line 311) spreads `task.budget` to preserve warnedAt/escalatedAt — setTaskBudget.ts does the same, so the seeding path must too. Settings defaults are NOT centralized: initProject.ts writes a partial settings object and each consumer resolves its own default in code (see positiveInt/resolveTaskSizing in util/planSize.ts) — follow that pattern rather than adding pacePerStepMs to initProject.ts. validateSettingsUpdate uses rejectUnknownFields with an explicit allowlist, so a new field is invisible (and rejected) until it is added to BOTH the allowlist array and a validate*Value branch. Note staleWorkerTimeoutMs/reviewStaleTimeoutMs exist in ProjectSettings and in this repo's .moe/project.json but are missing from that allowlist — do not 'fix' them here, it is out of scope.
planningNotes.risks: 1) Global rails require the literal phrases 'error handling' and 'test' in plan text and forbid 'eval(', 'innerHTML', 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML', '__proto__' — keep them out of code comments and test strings. 2) Do not let an invalid EXPLICIT budget arg fall through to seeding; the invalidInput throw at line 312 must stay reachable. 3) `budget: {}` (present but no wallClockMs) currently skips the explicit block — that case must seed, so key the else-branch on whether updatePayload.budget was actually set, not on `params.budget === undefined`. 4) submit_plan can run in SPEED/CONTROL mode in other tests; use TURBO in the new describe and keep clearAllSpeedModeTimeouts() in afterEach or timers leak across files. 5) The JetBrains/VS Code settings dialogs do not expose this field — deliberately out of scope, project.json edit only. 6) Fresh tasks have metrics.firstClaimAt set at claim, so a seeded budget starts counting from first claim, not from plan approval; that is the intended semantic, do not change it.
